# Descriptions
@@ 1
Caster magically summons a first level, non-intelligent animal from the
surrounding area, which arrives at the end of the round. The GM will determine
the type of creature that answers the summons. If the creature can understand
the caster, the creature can be controlled through normal communication.
Otherwise, control is maintained only through concentration by the caster. If
the creature summoned is used for a task that is not dangerous (in its own
perception), the duration for this spell is 10 minutes per level. However, if
the creature is ever put into a dangerous situation, the duration immediately
drops to 1 round per level (which may already have expired).
@@ 2
As Summons I, except caster chooses two of the following options: a) the level
of the summoned creature is increased by one, b) an extra 1st level creature
can be summoned, or c) the duration can be doubled. The same option may be
chosen more than once.
@@ 3
The caster can attune himself to a small creature (of creature intelligence)
to serve as his familiar. The caster must obtain the creature through normal
means and cast this spell on the creature once per day for 2 weeks
(concentrating for 4 hours per day). The caster can then control the familiar
and view the world through its senses by concentrating on it (though the
familiar must be within 50 feet per level). See Section 10.2 in the EssenceC
ompanion for more information about True Familiars.
@@ 4
As Summons III, except 5 options are chosen.
@@ 5
The caster can make a semi-intelligent being a companion. The companion can be
no more than 50% of the casters mass. The companion cannot be more intelligent
than the caster. The relationship between the caster and the companion is not
magical (and the caster must strive to maintain good relations with the
companion or it will leave him). The relationship should be treated as a
parent/child relationship. The companion will almost always obey a “do not”
command (e.g., “Do not drink that potion”); but the companion may make a RR to
resist a ''do'' command (e.g., ''Go and steal the eggs from the chickens'').
The GM should determine when a command is a “do not” command and when a
command is a “do” command (i.e., the commands do not have to have “do” or “do
not” in them-it is the intent of the command that should be examined).
@@ 6
Caster issues a magical summons to the nearest intelligent fantastic creature
of no greater level than 4. If the creature fails its RR, it will do
everything within its power to move to the caster. If it hasn’t found the
caster in four days, it will abandon the summons. When the creature arrives,
it will not be hostile to the caster.
@@ 7
As Summons III, except 9 options are chosen.
@@ 8
As Summons III, except 12 options are chosen.
@@ 9
As Summons III, except 14 options are chosen.
@@ 10
As Fantastic Summons IV, except that the creature may be up to 6th level and
it will attempt to answer the summons for six days.
@@ 11
As Summons III, except 16 options are chosen.
@@ 12
As Companion I, except the companion can be up to 100% of the caster’s weight.
The companion can also be intelligent (but not as intelligent as the caster),
with the relationship being treated as a parent/young adult relationship.
@@ 14
As Summons III, except 20 options are chosen.
@@ 15
As Fantastic Summons IV. except that the creature may be up to 10th level and
it will attempt to answer the summons for ten days.
@@ 17
As Summons III, except 24 options are chosen.
@@ 19
As Companion I, except there is no size limitation. The companion can also be
very intelligent (but not as intelligent as the caster), with the relationship
being treated as one between equals, the companion acting on its own without
commands from the caster.
@@ 20
As Summons III, except 29 options are chosen.
@@ 25
As Fantastic Summons IV, except that the creature may be up to 20th level and
it will attempt to answer the summons for twenty days.
@@ 30
As Summons III except 39 options are chosen.
@@ 50
As Summons III- except 50 options are chosen.
